change.runtime: workflows2d.cpp owns native service lifetime, world sharing, stepping, scene handoff, tween settlement and Impl helpers.
change.bindings: lua_workflows2d.cpp keeps ordered Lua bindings, userdata, table conversions, tween-value conversion and reload cloning.
change.private_header: workflows2d_internal.hpp shares original Impl fields/declarations and tween state. Only the non-userdata state gets a shared hidden namespace identity.
change.tween_factory: Native follow() returns shared state; two Lua callbacks aggregate-wrap that value in the original anonymous LuaTween2D. No additional allocation or Lua wrapper is introduced. All three Lua userdata definitions and their namespace identities are retained.

configuration: Normal Release -O2 target flags, original PCH on, compiler cache/LTO off, KIN_DEV_FAST_SCRIPTING=OFF, mold. No optimization/safety reduction.

baseline_diagnostic.scope: Diagnostic instrumentation only, not included in timing comparisons.

paired_compile_method: Three observations/version/compiler in before/after, after/before, before/after order, stable source/private-header snapshots and matching target PCH/flags without instrumentation. Original combined source/final binding source on CPU 2; new native source on CPU 0; unchanged JSON control on CPU 4. At most three workers. No owned validation jobs overlap timing. This is a compilation-set measurement without archiving/linking or whole-project scheduling. Host activity, SMT siblings and frequency remain uncontrolled. Every sample/control/load is retained.
tradeoffs: The split reduces implementation edit scopes and exposes parallel work. Repeated frontend/templates can increase aggregate compiler CPU and simultaneous memory; per-child RSS is not combined concurrent peak memory. Shared private header edits compile two files. Game-main scope is unchanged. Do not extrapolate this compilation-set comparison to a precise clean/cumulative project gain or to single-worker builds.
real_edit_method: Three real trailing-comment edits of the original combined file and each final source, through canonical Clang hex_demo archive/link. Four workers pinned 0/2/4/6. Assert exactly one expected C++ output per edit, restore source bytes/nanosecond mtimes after each, then refresh both canonical objects from restored bytes.

runtime_probe.method: Same assertions-enabled -O2 probe object linked separately before and after for Clang/GCC. Five alternating processes/version/compiler on CPU 2, each 30 samples after three warmups. Measure binding 50 VMs, 400000 input calls, 100000 tween state calls, 1000 native steps at zero dt, 40000 controller table calls. Assert counts/states; probes are narrow, without full game/GPU/frame workloads. Initial prototype showed roughly twofold host-wide timing changes, so final probes use five processes/version; none are discarded.

prototype_named_userdata.reason_for_revision: The first split put LuaTween2D in a shared hidden namespace and left follow() returning that userdata. It passed tests but GCC compilation-set wall improvement was small and compiler CPU grew substantially. Final design keeps all userdata local to bindings and returns only shared native state across the boundary; no direct same-host prototype-vs-final causal speedup is claimed.

def build_dir(compiler='clang'):
    return base / ('kin-build-time-out' if compiler == 'gcc' else 'kin-build-time-clang')

def compile_args(name, obj, compiler='clang', source=None):
    build = build_dir(compiler)

def run(args, label, cwd=None, cpus=None, timed=False):
    command = (['taskset', '-c', cpus] if cpus else []) + list(map(str,args))
    if timed:
        command = ['/usr/bin/time', '-f', '{"wall_seconds":%e,"user_seconds":%U,"system_seconds":%S,"max_child_rss_kib":%M}', '-o', str(out/(label+'.stats.json'))] + command
    with (out/(label+'.log')).open('w') as log:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if result.returncode:
        print((out/(label+'.log')).read_text()[-8000:], flush=True)
        raise RuntimeError((label,result.returncode))
    return json.loads((out/(label+'.stats.json')).read_text()) if timed else None

def save(name,value):
